title: Pilih dunia visual SyntaxLab
question: Kunci arah visual untuk frontend baru: pilih arah yang ditugaskan, salah satu alternatif, atau minta putaran baru. Pilihan ini mengunci visual brief sebelum implementasi.

options.label: Workshop Field Manual
options.lineage: Exploded-view assembly sheets and workshop instruction manuals
options.thesis: Belajar terasa seperti merakit keterampilan: setiap konsep menunjukkan bagian, hubungan, dan langkah yang bisa langsung dicoba.
options.viewport: Landing page opens as a working lesson bench: course path at left, a large HTML example and live preview side by side, then a numbered first exercise below. The primary action sits on the active lesson sheet.
options.risk: Can feel too mechanical if callouts dominate the lesson text; diagrams must clarify structure, never decorate it.

raised.raise: Grid density becomes structural: each panel, callout and code row aligns to one measured unit, with the construction grid visible only where it helps read the example.
Progression becomes exact and legible: every lesson step has a numbered place and a clear previous/next path.
Every learning promise is paired with a real interface demonstration: the lesson preview, runnable code, or exercise itself.

options.label: Browser Workshop Bench
options.lineage: The browser’s developer-tools and live-preview workspace
options.thesis: The fastest route from curiosity to understanding is to change a line and see the page respond.
options.viewport: A full working canvas leads with a short lesson prompt, editable code and rendered result in one balanced three-part view; related practice waits below the fold.
options.risk: A familiar editor-first interface can make the learning sequence feel secondary.

options.label: Tabbed Acetate Manual
options.lineage: Section-tabbed technical manuals with clear acetate overlays
options.thesis: A lesson is a transparent layer: see its place in the course, then focus on one concept at a time.
options.viewport: A stepped course tab rail frames a clear lesson sheet; explanation and code sit on a single page with the active section colored and the exercise punched as the next step.
options.case: Strong identification with self-study manuals and the clearest course-to-lesson hierarchy; the tactile layers become functional wayfinding.
options.risk: Layer transparency can lower contrast or become a visual trick; keep reading surfaces fully legible.

options.label: Indexed Learning Signal
options.thesis: Turn the course catalog into a crisp index that gets learners to the next relevant page quickly.
options.viewport: A compact course index labels each route and active step, paired with a large featured lesson preview and one visible continue action.
options.case: Raises scanability and route clarity, but the vintage broadcast grammar identifies less strongly with today's self-taught beginner.
options.risk: Can read as retro novelty if the typographic index overwhelms lesson content.

options.label: Course Shelf
options.thesis: Let learners browse topics visually and reveal useful context when they focus a course.
options.viewport: One featured course takes the lead above compact horizontal course rails; keyboard or pointer focus expands a tile to reveal the course goal and first lesson.
options.case: Recognizable and easy to browse, but the discovery wall makes an ongoing learning task less direct than a manual or workbench.
options.risk: May encourage browsing instead of continuing a learning session.

options.label: Variable Specimen
options.case: A specimen is less recognizable to a programming beginner and puts type exploration ahead of learning concepts.
options.kept: Keep the source's immediate feedback discipline: every code edit should produce an understandable visible result.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.case: Its movement notation is unfamiliar for this audience and does not clarify code or course structure.
options.kept: Use its exact sequencing discipline in lesson order, active-step state, and previous/next navigation.

options.label: Claim and Proof
options.case: The marketing claim sequence is built for persuasion rather than the learner's recurring work.
options.kept: Pair product statements with real lesson or editor evidence; do not rely on unsupported claims.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar learning SaaS interface with a clear course catalog, focused lesson pages and an accessible editor.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional homepage hero and course-card grid with a clear start-learning action; lessons use standard content-plus-sidebar layout.
canonCard.risk: Familiar and efficient, but visually interchangeable with other learning products by design.
